headline: GOLD CRACKS $3,500 AS CORE PCE HITS 3.3% — COMEX Falls to 15-Month Low; December Fed Hike Fully Priced
snippet: October personal consumption expenditures data released November 25 came in hotter than expected — headline PCE at 3.8% and core PCE at 3.3% (versus the 3.2% forecast) — sending COMEX gold to a 15-month low below $3,500, trading near $3,479.90, down 2.4% on the session. The break below $3,500 completes a rout that has taken gold from its September record of approximately $5,580 to its lowest level since September 2025 in just two months; December Fed hike expectations are now fully priced at 100% with an additional 62 basis points by end-2027 reflected in futures. For junior gold miners on TSX-V and ASX, the $3,500 floor breach shifts the question from 'is this a bottom?' to 'where is the next support?', with technicians watching the $3,420–$3,450 zone.

headline: CHINA EXTENDS RARE EARTH EXPORT PAUSE TO JANUARY 2027 — USAR DROPS 6%, MP MATERIALS -3% AS TRUMP-XI SUMMIT LOOMS IN SHENZHEN
snippet: Rare earth equities sold off sharply on November 25 as China's extension of export control pauses on holmium, erbium, thulium, europium, and ytterbium to January 10, 2027 failed to reassure markets ahead of the Trump-Xi summit in Shenzhen, with USA Rare Earth (NYSE: USAR) dropping ~6% to $6.31 (down 47% YTD), MP Materials (NYSE: MP) falling 3% (down 31% YTD), and Critical Metals declining 5% (down 56% YTD). The extended pause creates a fresh cliff edge deadline just as US-China trade talks resume — investors fear a January 10 lapse would instantly cut supply to Western manufacturers of EVs, defence systems, and semiconductors who have no near-term alternative supply. For retail investors evaluating Western rare earth developers, the selloff creates deep discounts in stocks whose underlying assets become more strategically valuable every day China's controls remain in force.

headline: SILVER TUMBLES 4% ON PCE — Falls TWICE as Hard as Gold; Industrial Demand Premium Collapses Under Rate Pressure
snippet: COMEX silver fell approximately 4% on November 25 — nearly twice gold's 2.4% decline — as the hotter-than-expected PCE print hit silver's dual role as both a monetary and industrial metal; rising rate expectations weigh on silver's industrial demand component in addition to its safe-haven premium, making it systematically more volatile than gold in hawkish Fed environments. The asymmetric selloff illustrates a pattern seen in every late-cycle rate-hike environment since 2022: silver underperforms gold on hawkish Fed surprises by roughly 1.5-2x, only to outperform when rate expectations turn — a risk management note for retail investors holding TSX-V or ASX silver explorers heading into year-end financing season.

headline: K2 GOLD DRILLS 36.58m AT 2.40 G/T Au AT MOJAVE NEWMONT ZONE — 16.77m AT 4.11 G/T Included; California System Extends
snippet: K2 Gold (TSX-V: KTO) reported that drilling at the Newmont Zone of its Mojave gold project in California returned 36.58 metres at 2.40 g/t gold, including a 16.77-metre higher-grade core at 4.11 g/t gold — confirming lateral continuity adjacent to the company's Dragonfly discovery, which has previously returned 86.9 metres at 4.0 g/t gold from surface. Finding 2.40 g/t over 36+ metres in adjacent stratigraphy suggests Mojave has a larger mineralised footprint than the existing geological model implies; in a California jurisdiction with a known but navigable permitting pathway for oxide-gold deposits, expanding the grade-width inventory ahead of a resource update sustains investor conviction through a commodity price correction.

headline: BRIXTON METALS: 330m AT 0.23% CuEq AT CATALYST PORPHYRY — MAIDEN COPPER AT SENTINEL TARGET; BC Thorn Project Becomes Two-Zone System
snippet: Brixton Metals (TSX-V: BBB) reported from its Thorn Project in northwestern British Columbia that hole THN26-395 returned two overlapping porphyry intervals at the Catalyst zone — 123.00 metres at 0.22% copper-equivalent from 73 metres and 330.34 metres at 0.23% copper-equivalent from 210 metres depth — while the same program also returned maiden copper mineralisation at the adjacent Sentinel target, adding a second discovery area to the project. A 330-metre continuous porphyry interval is bulk-tonnage class in a BC district that includes Newcrest's Tatogga project to the northwest; opening Sentinel in the same season doubles the district-scale exploration story at a time when copper's supply fundamentals remain compelling despite November's price volatility.

headline: SILVER ELEPHANT HITS 215 G/T GERMANIUM AND 50% ZINC IN KENTUCKY — US Critical Defense Mineral Confirmed as China Controls Deepen
snippet: Silver Elephant Mining (TSX: ELEF) reported that drill core assays from the Robinson-Lasher zinc deposit in Kentucky returned up to 50.17% zinc in individual samples and 215.4 g/t germanium — a defence-critical semiconductor element currently subject to China's export licensing controls and essential for infrared optics, fibre optic cables, and semiconductor manufacturing. At a time when the same Trump-Xi summit agenda includes germanium supply chain concerns and China's export controls are driving Western procurement anxiety, a confirmed in-situ germanium occurrence at a US-jurisdiction zinc deposit gives the Robinson-Lasher project a critical minerals angle that extends well beyond its zinc economics — and attracts government procurement interest that standard mineral economics alone would not justify.

headline: LION ONE DRILLS 44.39 G/T GOLD OVER 2.0m IN NEW ZONE 500 — Fiji Underground Mine Opens High-Grade Target Outside Current Plan
snippet: Lion One Metals (TSX-V: LIO) reported that its first underground drill hole targeting Zone 500 at the Tuvatu Alkaline Gold Project in Fiji returned 2.0 metres at 44.39 g/t gold — a bonanza-grade interval confirming a new high-grade lode system outside the current mine plan boundary. Zone 500 sits below and sub-parallel to Tuvatu's main producing lodes, making it a potential mine life extension target; at 44.39 g/t — well above the resource average — the new zone suggests a structurally controlled high-grade corridor that could add both ounces and project economics to the next resource update at an already cash-flowing mine.

headline: ALGO GRANDE CONFIRMS GOLD-RICH SKARN BENEATH CERRO GRANDE PORPHYRY — 39.94m AT 1.4% CuEq; Sonora Mexico Two-System Discovery
snippet: Algo Grande Copper (TSX-V: ALGR) confirmed a gold-enriched skarn horizon at depth at Cerro Grande 1 in Sonora, Mexico, with hole AG-CG-PH2-004 returning 39.94 metres at 1.40% copper-equivalent including an 8.77-metre core at 2.30% CuEq — directly beneath the porphyry copper-molybdenum-gold system identified in earlier drilling. Discovering a gold-rich skarn beneath a porphyry body is consistent with Sonora's established metallogenic model (the same sequence that hosts Grupo México's Cananea mine) and adds a second economic metal system to the project — a geometry that often receives premium M&A attention from mid-tier producers who value dual-system optionality on a single land package.

headline: WESTWARD GOLD HITS 3.1m AT 4.33 G/T Au AT NEW SSD TARGET IN NEVADA — 7.6m Envelope at Toiyabe Hills; Battle Mountain Trend System Grows
snippet: Westward Gold (CSE: WG) reported that hole T2603 at the new SSD Target within its Toiyabe Hills property in Nevada's Battle Mountain mining trend returned 7.6 metres at 1.97 g/t gold, including a 3.1-metre higher-grade core at 4.33 g/t — the best single interval at the SSD Target to date. Toiyabe Hills sits in the same trend as Kinross' Round Mountain and multiple other operating Nevada gold mines; a 4.33 g/t opening result at a new target in a well-understood, low-sovereign-risk US jurisdiction is exactly the type of exploration data that justifies a focused follow-up drill campaign in the same season, particularly for a small-cap explorer seeking to establish geological context ahead of a resource-definition program.

headline: BCA RESEARCH CALLED GOLD EXIT BEFORE TODAY'S $3,500 BREACH — Prescient 'Take Profits' Vindicated by Hot PCE Print
snippet: Mitrade's November 25 analysis highlights that BCA Research — an independent macro investment research firm — issued a tactical 'take profits and exit' call on gold before the October PCE release, a recommendation now vindicated as COMEX gold broke $3,500 on a hotter-than-expected 3.3% core reading. BCA's call was premised on gold's September record above $5,500 having fully priced the defensive demand narrative and left the metal exposed to a monetary tightening surprise; for retail investors sitting on November losses in gold ETFs and mining positions, the retrospective timing of this institutional exit is a useful case study in how professional managers position for event risk differently from retail buy-and-hold strategies — and a reason to separate tactical and strategic gold positions.

headline: YTTRIUM'S 125-FOLD PRICE GAP HANGS OVER TRUMP-XI SHENZHEN SUMMIT — China's Cost Stranglehold Makes Western Rare Earth Economics Nearly Impossible
snippet: An OilPrice.com analysis published November 25 as the Trump-Xi summit convenes in Shenzhen lays out the yttrium price gulf: Western producers supply the same critical rare earth — essential for EVs, wind turbines, LEDs, and defence systems — at approximately 125 times China's domestic price, an economic reality that makes it structurally impossible for Western supply chains to compete on cost without sustained government subsidies or guaranteed procurement contracts. The piece argues China's combination of cheap processing, state pricing, and export control leverage is not merely tactical positioning but a nearly insurmountable structural advantage — and that any deal emerging from Shenzhen that lacks binding rare earth supply guarantees leaves Western manufacturers as exposed to Chinese supply disruption as they are today.
